name: resize-split
covers: The editor/preview splitter: dragging it moves the panes in the side-by-side layout, Toggle layout stacks the panes and the splitter then drags vertically, and toggling back restores the side-by-side layout (the layout is a persisted setting, so the script leaves it as it found it).

setup.shell:
printf '# Split

Some text so both panes have content.
' > "$SMOKE/split.md"

phases.name: side by side
phases.note: The splitter is role=separator with aria-label 'Resize editor and preview'. Drag it 150 px to the right with real pointer events (BAM drag with dx); its bounds must change. A drag that lands nowhere (window not on top, wrong coordinates) leaves the bounds equal and fails here.

checks.note: aria-pressed=true shows as the AT-SPI 'pressed' state (bad-ass-mcp collects it since 2026-11-09); other platforms' toggle states unverified, so Linux-only.

phases.name: stacked
phases.note: Same splitter, now horizontal between the editor (top) and preview (bottom): drag it 120 px down.

steps.note: The splitter's bounds differ from where the side-by-side drag left it: the layout really changed.

notes: Needs bad-ass-mcp with drag by target (from_target + dx/dy), get_bounds and expect_not (2026-11-09). The split ratio itself is not persisted, only the layout, so the only cleanup is the second Toggle layout; if the script fails between the two toggles the app is left stacked (vertical_layout = true in settings), so press Toggle layout once by hand. Linux run 2026-11-09 (SteamOS, WebKitGTK 2.54, GDK_BACKEND=x11): xdotool's XTEST pointer reaches the page's mousedown/mousemove handlers, and the toggle's aria-pressed is the AT-SPI 'pressed' state.
